structure: Part 2 (Start: notification type, origin and what are you importing), read at commit 04a073b (checkout HEAD). Read in full: the three DR2.1 view overrides app/views/design-release-2.1/notification-type.html (57 lines), origin-of-the-import.html (179) and what-are-you-importing.html (143); the root partial app/views/partials/region-of-origin-code-input.html (31); the reference lists app/data/countries.js (79), country-region-prefixes.js (44), commodities.js (295), commodities-germinal-products.js (151), commodities-0101-species.js (20), commodities-0102-species.js (28), commodities-01061900-species.js (123); app/utils/commodity-search-data.js (36); and app/routes.js lines 68-272, 402-435, 500-823, 1011-1037, 10586-10675 and 11105-11308. For context only (claimed only where they shape these three pages), also read routes.js helpers outside the range: ensurePrototypeNotificationReference and resetNotificationJourneySession (291-365), redirectIfNoOrigin and isFromHub (436-451), getJourneyFormAction/isJourneySoftSaveAction/getJourneySaveRedirect (1560-1586), getSectionContinueRedirect (1588-1602), isGerminalProductCommodity (832), generateDesignReleaseNotificationReference (7820-7844), and partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html for the button labels each page's options produce. Pages covered: GET /create-notification (reset and routing), GET and POST /notification-type, GET and POST /origin-of-the-import (country search, region of origin code with country prefix, internal reference), GET and POST /what-are-you-importing (commodity and species search, selection, removal, type filtering), plus the country list (27 member states, 11 territories, 3 crown dependencies), the 41-entry region prefix map, the 21 live-animal commodities, the 15 germinal-product commodities and the three species lists (3, 11 and 106 entries). Claims run page by page in journey order, then the reference lists. Not covered here: client-side search behaviour in app/assets (out of the source's scope; recorded as a gap), the notification-status partial's own content and the journey-form-actions partial's amend and template-review variants (other parts).

claims.statement: GET /create-notification clears the current notification journey from the session but keeps the address book additions, draft notifications, deleted notification references, submitted notifications, saved templates, deleted template ids and the per-version session nests.
GET /create-notification also clears any in-progress template creation flag.
In Design Release 2.1, GET /create-notification with no category in the query string sends the user to the notification type page (/notification-type).

GET /create-notification with a recognised category query (for example from a category dashboard) skips the notification type page: it records that the journey started from a category dashboard, starts the notification with that type, and sends the user straight to /origin-of-the-import.

Starting a notification sets its type, sets its status to Draft, clears the template-creation flag, gives it a new notification reference (in the design releases) and saves it as a draft notification.
claims.quote:
sessionData.notificationType = notificationType
  sessionData.notificationStatus = 'Draft'
  delete sessionData.isCreatingTemplate

  if (isDesignRelease2SessionData(sessionData)) {
    sessionData.notificationReference = generateDesignReleaseNotificationReference(sessionData)
  }

  persistDraftNotification(sessionData)

claims.statement: A new design-release notification reference has the form GBN-AG-26- followed by six random upper-case letters or digits, and is chosen so it does not clash with the fixed sample reference, the current reference, dashboard notifications, drafts or submitted notifications.
claims.note: Read for context; the generator sits outside this part's line ranges.

claims.statement: Outside Design Release 2.1, GET and POST /notification-type redirect to /create-notification: the notification type page exists only in DR2.1.
GET /notification-type clears any previous errors before showing the page.
The notification type page's heading, shown as the radio group's legend, is "What are you importing?".
claims.quote: html: 'About the consignment What are you importing?', isPageHeading: true,

claims.statement: The notification type page shows the caption "About the consignment" above its heading.
The notification type page's page name is "What are you importing?", the same as the commodity page that follows origin.
The notification type page offers five radio options, in this order: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products.

{ value: 'live-animals', text: 'Live animals' },
  { value: 'germinal-products', text: 'Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)' },
  { value: 'plants-for-planting', text: 'Plants for planting' },
  { value: 'potatoes', text: 'Potatoes (seed and ware)' },
  { value: 'wood-products', text: 'Wood products' }

claims.statement: None of the notification type options has hint text, and the radio group has no hint.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any hint property on the options or the govukRadios call.

claims.statement: The notification type page pre-selects the type already held for the notification.

When no type is stored, the notification's type is worked out from its selections: germinal products only means germinal products, and selected species that are all live-animal species means live animals; otherwise the type is empty.
If no notification type is selected, the page shows the error "Select what you are importing", both inline and in the error summary, linking to the notificationType field.
The notification type, origin and commodity pages show their errors in an error summary titled "There is a problem".

The server accepts a notification type given either as its value or as its display label (case-insensitive), and also recognises three types the page does not offer: products of animal origin or animal by-products, high-risk food or feed of non-animal origin, and plants, plant products or other objects.
claims.note: Those three types can arrive through the /create-notification category query; the radio page never offers them.

claims.statement: The notification type page has a single "Continue" button and no save-and-return-to-overview button or cancel link.

The notification type page's back link goes to the dashboard (/), or to /templates when the user is creating a template; the service navigation highlights Dashboard, or Templates when creating a template.
Choosing a notification type marks the journey as not started from a category dashboard.
Changing the notification type to a different one from before clears every selected commodity and species.
When creating a template, choosing a notification type stores the type, sets the status to Draft and sends the user to /templates/create instead of the origin page.

Choosing a notification type starts a new notification (reference, Draft status, saved draft) when there is no notification reference yet; when there is one, it updates the type and saves the draft again.
After a valid notification type is chosen, every type (including plants for planting, potatoes and wood products) goes on to /origin-of-the-import.
The three start pages show an Alpha phase banner reading "This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.", with the feedback link pointing at #.
claims.quote: html: 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.'

claims.statement: GET and POST /origin-of-the-import make sure the notification has a design-release reference (GBN-AG-26-...), generating one if it has none or has a reference in another format.

The origin page's back link goes to /templates/create when creating a template, to the category dashboard list for the notification's type when the journey started from a category dashboard, and otherwise to /notification-type.
The origin page and the commodity page show the notification status block (which carries the notification reference) above the form.
claims.note: The partial's content is another part's; the reference is passed as notificationReference to both renders.

claims.statement: The origin page has the caption "About the consignment" and the heading "Origin of the import", which is also its page name.
claims.quote:
About the consignment

Origin of the import

claims.statement: The origin page asks for the country of origin under the sub-heading "Country of origin".

The country of origin is chosen through a search box with the placeholder "Search for a country", a search button ("Search", visually hidden text) and a results list labelled "Country search results"; the chosen country is submitted in a hidden countryOfOrigin field.
The country search has a polite live region for announcing search status to screen readers.
The country search shows no hint text.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any hint element in the country form group.

claims.statement: The origin page asks "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?" with Yes and No radios.
claims.quote: Does the consignment have a region of origin code?

claims.note: No validation in this part's routes sets this error; see the gap on the region radio.

claims.statement: Answering Yes to the region of origin question reveals a region of origin code field beneath the Yes option; No reveals nothing.

claims.statement: The region of origin code input accepts at most 5 characters, with autocomplete and spellcheck turned off.
The region of origin code input shows the chosen country's two-letter prefix in front of it (hidden from screen readers), so the user types only the suffix.
The region prefix map is also sent to the page alongside the country list, so the prefix can follow the country the user picks.
claims.note: The client script that applies it is in app/assets, outside this source's scope.

claims.statement: Region of origin prefixes are the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the chosen country, one per member state: Austria AT, Belgium BE, Bulgaria BG, Croatia HR, Cyprus CY, Czech Republic CZ, Denmark DK, Estonia EE, Finland FI, France FR, Germany DE, Greece GR, Hungary HU, Italy IT, Latvia LV, Lithuania LT, Luxembourg LU, Malta MT, Netherlands NL, Poland PL, Portugal PT, Republic of Ireland IE, Romania RO, Slovakia SK, Slovenia SI, Spain ES, Sweden SE.
claims.quote: // ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 prefixes shown before the region of origin code suffix
claims.note: Greece is GR, not the EU's EL.

claims.statement: Territories take their parent state's prefix (Azores and Madeira PT, Canary Islands ES, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Reunion and Saint Martin FR), except Ceuta, which is XC, and Melilla, which is XL.
claims.note: Melilla line: 'Melilla (Spain)': 'XL',

claims.statement: The crown dependencies have their own prefixes: Guernsey GG, Isle of Man IM, Jersey JE.
With no country chosen, or a country missing from the prefix map, no prefix is shown.
The region of origin code suffix is trimmed and converted to upper case when saved.
With Yes, a country and a suffix, the full region of origin code is saved as prefix, hyphen, suffix (for example FR-ABC12); if the country has no prefix, the code is the suffix alone.
Answering No (or not answering) to the region of origin question clears any saved region of origin code and suffix.
claims.quote:
req.session.data.regionOfOriginCodeSuffix = regionOfOriginRequired === 'Yes'
      ? (regionOfOriginCodeSuffix || null)
      : null
    req.session.data.regionOfOriginCode = null

claims.statement: Answering Yes with a suffix but no country keeps the suffix but saves no full region of origin code.
claims.note: Follows from the else branch keeping the suffix when the answer is Yes but setting regionOfOriginCode to null.

claims.statement: When the page is shown again, the suffix field is filled from the saved suffix, or else from the saved full code with everything up to the first hyphen removed.
If Yes is chosen and no region of origin code is entered, the page shows the error "Enter the region of origin code", inline and in the summary, linking to the code input.

The origin page does not validate the country of origin: a user can continue with no country chosen, and no error message for a missing or invalid country is defined, although the view has a slot to show one.
claims.note: Looked in validateOriginOfImport and the POST handler (11178-11226): countryOfOrigin is passed in but never checked.

claims.statement: The origin page does not require an answer to "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?": no error message for a missing answer is defined, although the view has a slot to show one.
claims.note: Only the Yes-without-code case is validated.

claims.statement: The source gives no format rule for the region of origin code suffix beyond the 5-character limit on the input: no allowed characters, minimum length or server-side length check.

The origin page has an optional text field labelled "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)" with the hint "Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank."
claims.quote: text: "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)",
claims.note: Hint: "Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank."

claims.statement: The internal reference is trimmed and saved, or cleared when left blank; it has no validation.
The country of origin and region of origin answer are saved as soon as the origin form is posted, before validation, so they are kept even when the page shows an error.

req.session.data.countryOfOrigin = countryOfOrigin || null

claims.statement: The origin page normally shows a single "Save and continue" button, with no save-and-return-to-overview button and no cancel link.
claims.note: The "Save and continue" label is the partial's default continueText. In amend or template-review states the partial shows its own buttons (another part).

claims.statement: Saving the origin page with the "return to overview" or "return to review" action skips validation, saves the draft and goes to the notification hub or the review page.

A valid origin page continues to /what-are-you-importing, or back to the notification hub when opened from the hub, to the review page when opened from review, or to the template review when editing a template.
When the origin or commodity page is opened from the notification hub, the form carries from=hub so that saving returns to the hub.
Origin details count as complete only when a country is chosen and the region question is answered, and, when the answer is Yes, a region of origin code suffix is held.
claims.note: Used by status and hub logic in other parts; it is stricter than the page's own validation.

claims.statement: The commodity page can be opened without origin details: its guard against missing origin never redirects.
claims.note: The guard is called but is a stub; read for context, it sits just outside this part's line range.

claims.statement: GET /what-are-you-importing makes sure the notification has a design-release reference and clears any leftover search text before showing the page.
The commodity page has the caption "About the consignment" and the heading "What are you importing?", which is also its page name.

claims.statement: In DR2.1 the commodity search lists only germinal-product commodities when the notification type is germinal products, and only live-animal commodities when it is live animals.

For plants for planting, potatoes, wood products, or no type, the DR2.1 commodity search has nothing to offer, so a user on those types cannot select a commodity and cannot pass the commodity page's validation.
claims.note: Inferred: getSearchCommodities returns an empty list for those types and validateCommoditySelection requires a selection. Those journeys look unbuilt beyond the origin page in this source.

claims.statement: Commodity search results are sorted alphabetically by commodity name, and each commodity's species are sorted by "common name (Latin name)", or by "commodity name (Latin name)" when a species has no common name.
Each commodity search entry offers the commodity's id, name, code and species, and each species its id, Latin name and (where it has one) common name.

claims.statement: The commodity page opens with the notification's existing selections already chosen, filtered to those that match the current notification type.

The commodity page has a "Help with commodity codes" details component explaining: "Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers." and "A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods."

Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers.

A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.

claims.statement: The commodity page uses the default journey buttons: "Save and continue", a secondary "Save and return to overview" button and a "Cancel and return to overview" link to the notification hub.
claims.note: Labels come from the partial's defaults: 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview', 'Cancel and return to overview'. Amend and template-review variants are another part's.

claims.statement: If nothing is selected, the commodity page shows the error "Select a commodity", inline and in the summary, linking to the commodity search box.

The commodity page accepts either selected species or a list of selections to pass validation, so a commodity selected with no species still passes, but only species are saved as the notification's selection.
claims.note: Inferred: applySpeciesSelectionToSession keeps only species ids, then the posted commoditySelections overwrite the records (11293-11296). hasCommoditySelection (1011-1013) counts species only, so such a notification would read as having no commodity elsewhere.

claims.statement: Submitted species and selections that do not belong to the notification's type are dropped before saving (for example, a germinal-product species on a live-animals notification).
A commodity belongs to germinal products if it is flagged as a germinal product; every other commodity belongs to live animals; for any other notification type, all commodities match.
Species ids that match no known species are dropped when the selection is saved.
Selected species may be submitted as a list, a JSON array, a single JSON string or a comma-separated string.
The saved selection records each selected species with its commodity id, commodity code and species id.
claims.quote:
type: 'species',
        commodityId: match.commodity.id,
        commodityCode: match.commodity.code,
        speciesId

claims.statement: The notification's main commodity (id, code and name) is the commodity of the first selected species; with no species it is cleared.
When every selected species is under commodity code 01061900 (cat, dog, ferret or other live mammals), any unweaned animals answer is cleared.

Saving the commodity page with the "return to overview" or "return to review" action skips validation, saves any valid species selection, saves the draft and goes to the notification hub or review page.

After a valid commodity selection, the user goes on to /reason-for-import, or back to the hub, review or template review as the entry point dictates; when creating a template, the user goes to the notification hub.
Removing a species from the selection also removes its number of animals, number of packages, net weight and package type.
Removing a commodity removes all of its selected species, along with each species' number of animals, number of packages, net weight and package type.
Removing the last selected species or commodity clears the notification's main commodity id, code and name.
A selected commodity is summarised as "code (name)", for example "0102 (Cattle)".
A selected species is titled "code (common name - Latin name)", using the commodity name when the species has no common name, for example "0102 (Domestic cattle - Bos taurus)".
A species' label in a list of selected species is its Latin name, or its common name when it has no Latin name.
Species and commodities are looked up across both the live-animal and germinal-product lists together, by id.

A commodity looked up by code returns the first commodity with that code, although several commodities share codes (cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals share 01061900; most germinal products share 05119985).
